_comment: Skills whose trigger-probe status (`never` / `STALE`) is KNOWN and ACCEPTED, read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/case_coverage.py's P004. Probing costs live model calls (~$0.05/probe, $6.86 for a 105-case corpus sweep), so a hard failure on `never probed` would be a check no round could clear without a spend it may not have budgeted -- and a checker that can never go green gets uninstalled. An entry silences P004 for that skill. It must name an `owner` (the track that will pay for the probe) and a `why`; an entry with no owner, an entry naming a skill that no longer exists, and an entry for a skill that HAS since been probed under its current description are all P005 ERRORS, because an acknowledgement that outlives its debt is a mute button. EMPTY as of round 357, which probed all 27 skills in the corpus for the first time (state/trigger-eval/round-357-full-corpus.{json,md}); the file exists so the schema is documented and so the next round that must defer a probe has somewhere to say so.

newest-snapshot-is-not-the-record.why: New in round 490 (NUC-integration E), registered unprobed under the standing convention rounds 373/375/377/378/379/394/395/398/401/402/406/407/412 all used: a probe is a priced run and belongs to a skills(B) batch, and a round probing its own fresh paraphrase scores its own wording. Round 490 had no operator authorisation for a spend. Following round 405's measured finding (5 of 5 by-reading sibling guesses were wrong), this names NO confusable to rewrite toward. What it names instead is a scorable prediction: I predict nsr-far (`I diffed two copies of the same rotated log file and they disagree on the last line`) is the WEAKEST of the three positives, because its surface is a corruption question and the description leads with snapshot-selection language, and the connective -- that a trailing summary row is computed over the rows present, so honest reads of one growing file MUST differ there -- is the skill's content rather than its trigger. I predict the most likely non-abstention taker on nsr-far is a debugging or provenance skill rather than a data-selection one. Both are by-reading guesses and round 405 says such guesses lose; score them, do not rewrite toward them. The negative case nsr-neg-one-snapshot expects NO skill: there is exactly one snapshot and no analysis reading from it, so a description that fires on it is matching the word `snapshot` rather than the situation. Probe nsr-near/mid/far, then run `displacement.py claims --only <that round's runs>` and let the measurement name the taker. Re-derive rho before sizing the batch rather than quoting round 405's 0.143 or round 393's 0.333.

losses-name-their-winner.why: New in round 405 (skills B) -- authored by the round that PAID this file's seven-round batch, and deliberately not probed by it. (2) More usefully: this skill's own subject says the confusable you NAME is not the one that wins, so naming its nearest sibling here would be the exact error it documents. What it does instead is name the MEASURABLE prediction -- run `displacement.py claims --only <the probing round's runs>` afterwards and see which skill actually takes lntw-near/mid/far. Its negative case lntw-neg-replicate deliberately expects repeats-are-not-replicates, which is the one genuine boundary (that skill answers 'did the loss replicate', this one answers 'who won'); repeats-are-not-replicates had a BODY-ONLY upgrade this round, so its digest ebd7016b65db is unchanged and round 393's probe of it still applies. _round_447_note: Round 447 (skills B) PRICED this batch -- round 435's next-step 4, deferred by rounds 436, 445 and 446 -- and in doing so corrected the number they were pricing. This map holds 26 skills, not the SIXTEEN the note above carries, and the undercount decomposes exactly: round 435's note counted the FOURTEEN entries that round registered and dropped the nine already in the map from rounds 405-421, and the entry round 436 added (matcher-defines-the-population) was never counted at all, so the carried arithmetic ran 14 -> 15 (r445) -> 16 (r446) against a true 23 -> 24 -> 25 -> 26. THE PRICE, derived from this batch's own cases rather than a corpus average: every one of the 26 entries has at least three positive cases in skills/trigger-cases.json (91 across the batch, none missing -- so round 435's `no positive cases at all` blocker is closed, not carried), and round 405's measured whole-batch payment was 41 cases / 205 probes / $11.97, i.e. 5.00 probes per case and $0.0584 per probe. 91 x 5 = 455 probes = $26.57. Round 405's per-SKILL average brackets that from above at 26 x $1.33 = $34.58, higher because the nine entries round 405 paid averaged 4.56 cases against this batch's 3.5; the per-case figure is the estimate because it is derived from the cases that will actually be sent. The quoted sixteen prices out at $16.35 on the same arithmetic, so the real batch is 62% larger and $10.22 dearer than the standing ask. It still needs operator authorisation and this round did not have it. What this round removes is the excuse that nobody knew the size. Found by selfdesc_check's J005 the first round it was allowed to read a `_round_NNN_note` field at all -- knowledge/round-447-the-count-that-no-checker-could-read.md.

_round_450_note:
Round 450 (language C) added ONE entry, its own new skill, and did not pay the batch -- the THIRTEENTH consecutive round of growth since round 405 emptied it. It also did the one thing round 449's note asked for, which is to re-derive rather than carry: the batch is 29 by count at this commit and the price is $29.20, not round 447's $26.57 and not round 449's 'floor, not a quote'. THE DERIVATION, re-run rather than scaled: 100 positive cases in skills/trigger-cases.json name a skill in this map (up from round 447's 91, taken over a 26-entry map), x5 probes = 500 probes, at round 447's measured $0.0584/probe = $29.20. Re-derive both halves with:
  python3 -c "import json; reg=json.load(open('state/known-unprobed-skills.json'))['skills']; cases=json.load(open('skills/trigger-cases.json')); pos=[c for c in cases if set(c.get('expect') or []) & set(reg)]; print(len(reg),'skills',len(pos),'cases','$%.2f'%(len(pos)*5*26.57/455))"
The rate itself is the one number NOT re-derived this round -- it is round 447's, from a run this round did not repeat -- so it is the half to distrust first. Operator authorisation is still the only missing input, and it is now a $29 authorisation rather than a $27 one; the growth is 3 rounds of +1 skill and +9 cases since it was priced.

_round_457_note: Round 457 (harness A) added a single registration, for the skill it authored (`writer-lands-its-own-write`), and did not pay the batch. It also CORRECTS the shape round 451 carried. Re-derived from the two files rather than carried: the batch was 31 skills / 106 positive cases AT ROUND 457, and at round 447's still-unre-measured $0.0584/probe over round 451's 5 invocations per case that is $30.95, against round 451's 30 / 103 / $30.07. The correction is the GROWTH RATE. Round 451 called itself "the FOURTEENTH consecutive round of growth since round 405" and priced the trend at roughly $0.88 a round. That trend ENDED at round 452: `git log -- state/known-unprobed-skills.json` shows round 451 was the last commit to touch this file before this one, so rounds 452 through 456 added nothing and the run of consecutive growth stopped at fourteen. Over the six rounds 452-457 the batch grew by a single registration, three cases and $0.88 TOTAL — about $0.15 a round, not $0.88. An operator deciding whether to authorise now rather than later should use the smaller number, and should note that the rate itself ($0.0584/probe) is still round 447's and is now ten rounds old with no round re-measuring it. Operator authorisation remains the only missing input.

_round_477_note: Round 477 (skills B) PRICED this batch before adding to it -- research-state.md's round-435 item 4 -- and got it wrong on the first attempt in a way worth recording. The first draft priced the sweep at $0.05/probe, the rate in this file's `_comment`. That constant is not the measured rate: `_round_457_note` carries $0.0584 per INVOCATION at 5 invocations per case, i.e. $0.292/case, which is 5.8x the header. Reading the artefact's oldest self-description instead of its newest measurement is exactly what round 463's note warned about ('that per-probe rate is now SIXTEEN rounds old -- re-derive it before pricing the sweep rather than quoting it'), and this round could not re-derive it either, because re-deriving a price requires the priced run. So the honest figure, with its provenance: AT ROUND 477 the batch was 41 entries and 136 positive trigger cases, which at round 447's $0.292/case is $39.71 for the batch and $98.30 for the whole 412-case corpus -- both at a rate now TWENTY-TWO rounds unmeasured, so read them as the order of magnitude and not as quotes. The count is written in the past tense and scoped to this round, per `_round_458_note`'s fix and `_round_459_note`'s rule; the non-staling reading is `len(json.load(open(...))['skills'])`. What the state file carries is FOURTEEN, from round 435, still quoted as 'the fourteen-deep probe batch' in round 475's item 11 -- and the correction was never missing: `_round_450_note` re-derived 30 here twenty-seven rounds ago and `_round_463_note` 35, and neither number reached research-state.md. A registry that re-derives a quantity and a state file that carries one are two records of the same thing with no reconciliation between them. Round 477 had no operator authorisation for a priced run and did not make one. It also REWROTE `derived-subject-set`'s description, and measured that cost rather than assuming it -- case_coverage over the same tree, before and after: probed 51/98 -> 50/98, replicated 31/98 -> 30/98, cross-report verdicts disagreeing 49 of 103 -> 47 of 99, POOLED REFUTED 5 -> 4. The last is the one to read: that skill was one of only five whose description had been measured and REFUTED, so the edit removed a refutation of the old wording, not a confirmation. It is deliberately NOT registered in `skills` above -- P004 is about `never` and `STALE`, the live finding is a P009 warning about an unreplicated weak-probe draw, and an entry silencing the wrong code is the mute button this file's `_comment` forbids. Two cases were added for the round-477 bounded-exception section (`dss-static-reader`, `dss-desc-claims-the-pattern`), taking that skill from 4 positive cases to 6, so the debt priced above grew by $0.58 in the same round -- stated rather than netted out.
